scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): agrees that laws cannot change hearts, then argues they still do great good; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: A law can punish bad behaviour, but it cannot easily make people kinder or wiser.
One claim holds that many problems of modern society cannot be solved by laws, on the reason that laws cannot change what is in people's hearts and minds.
I largely agree that laws alone cannot solve every problem, but I believe they still do far more good than the claim suggests.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why laws cannot change hearts

sentences.text: First, it is true that some problems lie beyond what any law can reach.
Laws can forbid actions, but they cannot force people to feel respect, honesty, or kindness.
For example, a law against prejudice cannot, by itself, remove the hatred in a person's heart.
This shows that deep social problems often grow from attitudes that no rule can simply erase.
People may obey a law outwardly while keeping the very feelings that caused the problem.
Real change in hearts and minds usually comes from education, example, and culture, not from force.
To this extent, the reason behind the claim is genuinely sound.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why laws still do much

sentences.text: Second, however, it is wrong to conclude that laws cannot help solve these problems at all.
Even if laws cannot change hearts directly, they can change behaviour and protect people from harm.
Consider how laws against unfair treatment have slowly changed what people accept as normal.
Such laws show that rules can shape attitudes over time, not just control actions.
Laws also set a clear standard that teaches each new generation what a society values.
Without laws, even good intentions would struggle to protect the weak or punish the cruel.
Laws, then, are a vital part of the solution, even if they are not the whole of it.
In conclusion, laws alone cannot reach the hearts and minds behind many social problems.
But they still change behaviour, protect people, and slowly shape attitudes for the better.
The wisest societies use laws alongside education and example to solve their deepest problems.
